title: DevExp mini-retreat notelet: quickstarts, SDKs, and examples archaeology
body:
Context: 2-hour internal mini-retreat focused on lowering first-success time for new engineers and external devs using Redwood. Goal was to triage the quickstart surface (hello world, embeddings, chat, and function-calling flows), identify low-effort wins, and capture medium-risk changes that need broader review.

Attendees: Aisha (facilitator), Ben, Samir, Ruth, Diego, Maya (PM, joined for first 30m).

High-level observations:
- Quickstart activation funnel: local dev -> token & env -> run sample. Last-click success rate measured from telemetry: ~42% (users who reached code run). We want 60% within 6 weeks.
- Most failures are environment/config errors (API key env var naming), mismatched SDK versions, and missing example config for private deployments.
- Samples garden has many orphaned examples: 12 examples not run in >6 months. Some depend on internal fixtures (should be rewritten).
- SDK churn: 0.18% breaking changes per week surfaced by CI failures on examples. Many are minor but create friction for quickstarts.

Key decisions (agreed during session):
1) Standardize env var name to REDWOOD_API_KEY across all quickstarts and update docs 1-pager. (owner: Ben, eta: 2026-01-20)
2) Add a lightweight "local smoke test" script (node/python) that runs a stubbed call to the hosted API and exits with clear error codes for common failures. Ship as part of starter-kit. (owner: Samir, eta: 2026-01-22)
3) Prune or flag samples older than 6 months. Move flagged samples into /examples/archived with READMEs stating why they were archived. (owner: Ruth, eta: 2026-01-28)
4) Create a canary CI job that runs 6 representative quickstarts on each SDK change (mac/linux, node/python). Fail the PR early with actionable logs. (owner: Diego, eta: 2026-02-05)

Action items (concrete):
- Ben: write the env var migration guide + small compat shim to accept REDWOOD_API_KEY or OLD_RE_API by default for 4 weeks. Post as PR and ping #devexp. (blocked? no)
- Samir: prototype smoke-test script (node + python wrappers), include instructions for use in CI and local dev. Add exit codes doc. (needs review from SRE on networking assumptions)
- Ruth: run a samples audit script (list examples, last-run, deps) and produce CSV; mark archive candidates and create tickets for rewrite where ROI > medium. (ETA: 1 week)
- Diego: set up canary CI matrix and integrate with PR template; include test artifacts upload. (needs runner quota allocation from infra)
- Aisha: update quickstart landing doc with "first 5 minutes" checklist and micro-copy for token errors. (will reference new smoke-test)

Blockers / Risks:
- Infra runner capacity: canary CI requires additional ephemeral runners for matrix runs. Raised ticket ENGOPS-492. If delayed, we fallback to nightly canaries but that delays feedback.
- Private deployment examples: we don’t have a standard local stub for on-prem auth. Risk: customers with Private will still hit friction; plan is to add explicit section and sample env file for private in next sprint.
- Telemetry gaps: activation funnel includes anonymous events; need to ensure privacy-safe tagging before further analysis. (privacy review queued)

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- "examples archaeology" sprint: schedule a 2-day paired work session to rewrite 10 highest-impact samples. Invite solutions-eng for customer edgecases.
- Consider creating a minimal "hello-llm" binary (go/rust) that demonstrates embedding+chat in <40 lines for platform devs. Could be a good cross-language starter.
- Microcopy: change error messages to include exact troubleshooting steps (e.g., "No API key found; set REDWOOD_API_KEY or follow https://.../quickstart#token").

Metrics to watch (weekly):
- Quickstart run success rate (post-smoke-test adoption) — target +18pp in 6 weeks.
- PRs blocked by canary CI before merge — target reduce broken mainline by 50% in quarter.
- Number of archived examples vs rewritten — aim to keep <5 archived at any time.

Follow-ups / calendar:
- Sync at weekly DevExp standup (Tue 10:00) — quick status updates on the four owners above.
- Pairing session: "examples archaeology" — Wed 2026-01-20 13:00-16:00 (invite Maya + solutions eng).
- Retro checkpoint after first canary run: 2026-02-08.

Unresolved questions:
- Do we accept both env var names permanently or run a 4-week shim then remove? (Decision leaning to shim then remove; confirm with PM/legal on docs.)
- What is the budget for CI runners for the team next quarter? Need finance input.

Appendix (quick links and scratch):
- Quickstart landing draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEVEXP/Quickstart+Landing (draft)
- Example audit script (local): scripts/examples-audit.sh (WIP in repo)
- Jira tickets created: ENG-3456 (canary ci), ENG-3461 (smoke-test), ENG-3472 (samples audit)

Scratch:
- TODO: fetch telemetry segment breakdown tomorrow.
- Note: Maya asked for a one-pager for sales when we move quickstart to "official".

End of notelet.

(Informal — helpful to copy into Confluence later once owners confirm.)
